thread:
maria: Heads up: eu-south control plane started returning intermittent 503s around 09:42 UTC. I see a flurry of controller-manager restarts and an etcd leader re-election loop.
kevin: Saw it too. Pod scheduling stalled, GPU pool scaleouts failing and AttachQueue is spiking.
anika: Provisioner logs show repeated netlink errors + attach timeouts. Grabbed a grep: 
```
grep -i "attach queue" /var/log/provisioner/*.log | tail -n 20
2026-04-23T09:42:12Z provisioner: attach queue wait >30s for vm-rtx-12
2026-04-23T09:42:18Z kernel: netlink: RTM_DELROUTE error -110
```
opsbot: Alert: apiserver 5xx rate exceeded threshold in eu-south (09:42-09:47 UTC). Auto-escalation triggered.
lucas: Did anyone touch egress/NAT in eu-south last night? I rolled a small ACL change around 02:00 but thought it was limited to controlplane-bastion.
maria: Possibly related. Also seeing etcd WAL fsync latency spikes on nvme for the leader: iops > 95th pct. Correlating with attach failures now.
kevin: Quick checks: `kubectl -n kube-system get pods` on controlplane nodes and `kubectl logs` for controller-manager. If lease renewals time out controller-manager will restart.
anika: Paste from controller-manager logs: 
```
I0423 09:42:15.123456      1 leaderelection.go:360] failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
E0423 09:42:15.123467      1 server.go:200] failed to start controllers: failed to renew lease
```
maria: Doing a quick canary: bumped controller-manager replicas 1->3 in eu-south-canary to reduce single-point-of-failure while we investigate.
lucas: If leader flaps, provisioner can't attach GPUs -> upstream client requests time out. Can we throttle attach retries until KV cache warms or reduce concurrency?
oncall-sre: I've toggled the provisioner feature flag to disable aggressive attach retries for eu-south (`--attach-retry=linear-10s`) and set token backoff. Monitoring for 20m.
kevin: :thumbsup: Also open a cloud provider ticket for nvme iops degradation in eu-south and include the WAL fsync profiles. Logging link: https://redwood-infra/logs/3201234567 (internal)
anika: Adding cost note: keeping 3 controller-manager replicas in canary increases reserved node usage (and GPU reservation if co-located). Short-term customer impact > cost, but track burn.
maria: Agreed. If stable for 30m we'll keep canary, then do a controlled rollback of the egress ACL if the provider finds no hardware issue. Creating incident. /incident create "eu-south controlplane thrash: nvme iops + egress ACL suspected"
opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-eusouth-ctrlplane
lucas: Next steps: provider ticket, consider moving etcd WAL to isolated volume (separate nvme stripe) in eu-south, and add guardrail to throttle GPU attach concurrency when apiserver 5xx rate > 5%.
oncall-sre: Observability update: apiserver 5xx rate down ~90% over the last 15m since throttles + canary. Keeping mitigations in place. Will update incident and reopen if we see reoccurrence.
